best_for: Windows users who want their passwords in one encrypted file they control, with no cloud account, and who like adding features through plugins.

points.title: One file, no cloud
points.text: Your passwords live in a single encrypted database file. You can move it between computers or keep it on a USB stick. Nothing is stored on a vendor's server because there is no vendor service.

points.title: Strong locks, your choice of key
points.text: The database is encrypted with AES, ChaCha20 or Twofish, and Argon2 slows down guessing attacks. Unlock it with a master password, a key file or both.

points.title: Auto-Type fills logins
points.text: A global hotkey types your user name and password into the active window, in a sequence you can change. Fields can also be dragged into other windows.

points.title: Plugins fill the gaps
points.text: KeePass itself is lean. Browser autofill, passkey support and extra import formats come from plugins. It can import from over 35 formats out of the box.

points.title: Installer, portable or MSI
points.text: Setup needs administrator rights, but KeePass runs without them afterward. The portable ZIP needs no install at all. The MSI is meant for network administrators. Builds cover x86, x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Windows first
points.text: KeePass is a Windows app. It can run on Linux and macOS through Mono, with extra packages for Auto-Type, and the project itself points to alternatives such as KeePassXC. The Windows listing keeps 22 versions.
